decisionsTitle: Tests read their fixture's calendar, never the day they run: `yarn test:clock`
decisionsSection:
**What happened.** On 2026-10-11 at 07:00Z the pre-commit hook of a release batch went red on `tests/integration/registrations/family-declarations.test.ts` › «Semnez mai târziu on the opened link's own person…», which had passed that morning. Its fixture race started at `2026-10-11T07:00:00Z`; the skip it pressed (`skipFamilyDeclaration`, which takes `now`) reads its link through `readRegistrationTokenContext`, which takes `new Date()`. Once the real clock passed the race, the link was refused. Nothing in the release touched it: the calendar did. GitHub now requires `docs-check`, `tested-tree` and `e2e` on `qa` and `main`, so such a test blocks a release on the morning its date comes.

**Decision.** A test that writes a date either hands that date to everything it calls as `now`, or pins the real clock to it around the call that reads `new Date()` — never lets code compare a fixture date with the day the suite runs. Three pieces make that checkable:

- `yarn test:clock` (`scripts/test-clock.mjs`) runs the unit and database suite with the real clock moved forward — by default +1 month, +1 year and +10 years, two workers — and names every test that fails there. The move is `tests/helpers/shifted-clock.mjs`, loaded only while `TEST_CLOCK_AT` is set: every argument-less `new Date()`, `Date()` and `Date.now()`, and PGlite's own `now()`, read the moved date, while a date the test writes stays as written. It also loads through `NODE_OPTIONS=--import` in every Node process the run starts, on one offset, so a script a test spawns reads the same clock as the test (the first version did not, and `release-from-branch.test.ts` failed for that reason alone).
- `atTheClock(instant, work)` (`tests/helpers/clock.ts`) fakes `Date` alone, standing at `instant` until `work` returns or settles — timers stay real, so PGlite runs as usual. A page, a route, a Server Action, the proxy or a link's read is called at the fixture's own instant; a file whose tests also time things from `Date.now()` pins `Date` in `beforeEach` instead (the house pattern of `job-throttle.test.ts`).
- `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` § Tests that the calendar breaks says the practice, the commands, the order of the fixes, and what the run cannot reach.

**What it found** — the baseline (`yarn test` at today's clock, 2026-10-11 11:21Z): 11 663 passed, 1 failed, the family declaration above, already gone off. With the clock moved: 66 tests in 18 files, by the day each would have gone red: `club-copy.test.ts` (the race of 2026-10-11 ends that evening: the registration page's email state asks the database's `now()` whether the race is ahead); the register page rendered by `form-helpers`, `health-note-form`, `kit-shirt-form` and `register-page-resting` (registration closes 2026-11-20: the page 404s); the five `start-list-*` files (race 2026-11-21: the list goes empty); `minimum-age.test.ts`'s staff form action (2026-11-21); `members-only.test.ts` (the members' run of 2027-03-14); `answer-corrections.test.ts` (a row's `answers_written_at` left to its default, 2028–2030), `sponsor-list.test.ts` (a sixteen-year-old turns eighteen, 2028-05-05), `calendar-month-from-path.test.ts` (the proxy names months two years either way: 2029-01-01), the guardian rule in `minimum-age` and `minors` (2029–2030), and `event-draft-preview.test.ts` (2030-10-07). Every one is fixed in the test, its fixture's dates and their distances unchanged. The rerun at the three dates: zero.

**Reported, not changed — `src/` reads of the real clock that ignore a `now` the caller passed:** `readRegistrationTokenContext` (`token-actions.ts`), read by `skipFamilyDeclaration` and `withdrawFromFamilyWizard`, which take `now`; the email state of the registrations list, the registration page and the desk (`email-state.ts`: `stateSql` → `openRefusalsWhere()` with no `now`, so the database's `now()`), under `listRegistrationsForAdmin` and `findRegistrationDetailForAdmin`, which take `now`; the guardian rule in `fields.ts` (`isMinorOn(birthDate, new Date())`), under `submitRegistration`, `createRegistrationByStaff` and `editRegistrationAnswers`, which take `now` — its comment says today is deliberate. A request reading its own clock is right in production; only a test notices, and threading `now` through is the owner's call.

**Not reachable by `test:clock`, read by hand:** `tests/concurrency/` runs against a real PostgreSQL whose `now()` is the real one — `capacity.test.ts` submits with `new Date()` (the seeded privacy notice is effective from the day it was seeded) against a race starting `2026-12-01T09:00Z`, so it goes red by then; the other files pass `NOW` explicitly and their paths compare nothing with the real clock. `tests/e2e/` creates events on written dates from `2027-04-14` (`group-run-declaration`) and `2027-04-17` (`partner-marker`) through `2027-11-17` (`night-event`), `cms-publish` and a dozen others in May–September 2027: after each date its event is past and a spec that expects an open door or an upcoming card fails. The seeds draw their dates from today (`sample-dates.ts`, §162) and never age. None of these changed here.

**Refused.** Changing `src/` to take `now` in those three places (behaviour, not a test fix — reported instead). Moving the fixtures to 2099 (it moves the bomb, and a minor's birth date with it). Relative dates from `Date.now()` in the fixtures that pin dates (a test then means something different each day). `test:clock` inside `yarn check` (three full runs: about twenty minutes each on two workers).
changelogLine: - **Tests no longer go red on a calendar date** — `yarn test:clock` runs the suite with the clock a month, a year and ten years ahead; the 66 tests it found, which would have failed from tonight, 20–21 November, 14 March 2027 and later, now read their own fixture's date. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given `yarn test:clock`, when it runs the unit and database suite with the real clock moved to +1 month, +1 year and +10 years (`TEST_CLOCK_AT`; every Node process of the run on one offset, a written date left as written), then no test fails that passes under `yarn test`: a test whose path reads the real clock calls it at the fixture's own instant (`tests/helpers/clock.ts`). Verification: unit `scripts/test-clock.test.ts`; the three runs (2026-10-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
